:::{#def-sine}
#### Sine

For a real number $\angpar$, the second coordinate of the point reached from $(1, 0)$
by moving a distance $\abs{\angpar}$ along the unit circle (@def-cosine)
is the **sine** of $\angpar$, written $\sin\angpar$.

:::

{{< slidebreak >}}

:::{#exm-sine}
#### Sines of some angles

- $\angpar = 0$ stays at $(1, 0)$, so $\sin 0 = 0$.
- $\angpar = \pi$ goes half way around the circle, to $(-1, 0)$, so $\sin\pi = 0$.
- $\angpar = \pi/2$ goes a quarter of the way round, to $(0, 1)$, so $\sin(\pi/2) = 1$.
- $\angpar = \pi/4$ reaches the point with $x_1 = x_2 = \tfrac{1}{\sqrt{2}}$ (@exm-cosine),
  so $\sin(\pi/4) = \tfrac{1}{\sqrt{2}}$.

:::
